newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Sidanko seeks to attract $3 bln in new investment.
newsitem.headline: Sidanko seeks to attract $3 bln in new investment.

text.p: Russia's NK Sidanko oil group seeks to attract $3 billion in investment over the next few years, including $500,000-$700,000 this year, a senior company official said on Thursday.
"We are in the process of talking to potential investors, and rather major ones," Sidanko Vice President Ziya Bazhayev told Reuters.
Bazhayev did not detail the plans or say who the investors were, but he said details would be made public soon.
Sidanko shareholders decided at an emergency meeting last December to raise the company's charter capital from 9.30 billion roubles to 26.17 billion roubles.
Igor Antonov, Deputy Chairman of the Board of Uneximbank told a news conference the company could issue stock on international markets or simply sell oil to raise extra investment funds.

Uneximbank (Oneximbank in Russian), along with Bank MFK, are part of the large Interros-oil closed stock company, which acquired at least 85 percent of Sidanko shares through the government's controversial 1995 shares-for-loans programme.
"This (investment) could simply be credits financed through a range of mechanisms, including shares issued on international markets, or by shipments of oil and oil derivatives," said Antonov.
He said the plans were being worked out between bank and company experts.
Sidanko is one of Russia's largest vertically integrated oil groups. Its other holdings include Chernogorneft, Varyoganneftegaz and Kondpetroleum.
